title: Bony cavity boundaries · OUVC 10503

source.name: Ohio University · WitmerLab
source.acquisition: CT, 625 µm slice thickness, GE LightSpeed Ultra Multi-Slice, 120 kV, 200 mA
source.scale_note: The U3D unit-scale field is zero. Native coordinates are multiplied by 10 for display; viewer coordinates are not calibrated physical measurements.
source.modifications: Decoded every source triangle at full detail; separated the two disconnected inferior conchae without changing geometry; retained source dental-arch grouping; rigidly rotated, centered and uniformly scaled for display; computed smooth surface normals. No decimation, subdivision, geometric smoothing, synthetic pores or registration to another subject.

placement: Original same-specimen coordinates, rotation and skull-centering translation. No registration or reshaping.
representation: Surfaces outline spaces enclosed by bone. They are not additional solid bones or soft tissues. Bilateral resource groupings are retained.

structures.name: Frontal sinuses
structures.description: The segmented air spaces inside the frontal bone, above the orbits. This surface outlines the cavity against its bony walls.

structures.name: Maxillary sinuses
structures.description: The paired air spaces in the maxillae, below the orbital floors and above the upper dental arches. Their original bilateral source grouping is retained.

structures.name: Ethmoidal air cells
structures.description: The labyrinth of air cells within the ethmoid between the nasal cavity and the medial orbital walls. The surface follows the original segmented cavity boundaries.

structures.name: Sphenoidal sinus
structures.description: The segmented air space within the body of the sphenoid, behind the nasal cavity and below the sella turcica.

structures.name: Mastoid air cells
structures.description: The communicating air spaces inside the mastoid portions of the temporal bones. These are the specimen's original cavity surfaces, rather than additional bones.

structures.name: Bony labyrinth cavities
structures.description: The original segmented inner-ear cavity boundaries in the petrous temporal bones, including the cochlear and semicircular regions. The surface depicts spaces enclosed by bone, not soft inner-ear tissues.
